item.title: Dialysis scandal: No patient has ever been dialysed on mats, floor – LUTH CMD
item.description: By Chioma Obinna & Blessing Oghene The Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH) yesterday dismissed as false a viral social media video alleging that patients were being subjected to dialysis treatment on mats and floors at its facility, insisting that no patient had ever received such treatment at the hospital. Chief Medical Director of LUTH, Prof. Wasiu Adeyemo, who gave the clarification during a media briefing and tour of the hospital’s Lion Isaac Olusola Dada Dialysis Centre and Renal Institute in Lagos, described the allegation as misleading and damaging to the hospital’s reputation. Adeyemo expressed disappointment that a major television station broadcast the video without first contacting the hospital to verify the claims or obtain its response. “Nothing in LUTH is hidden. That’s why we showcase our activities every day, and you have access to us. It is quite unfortunate that somebody put something on social media and a major news outlet publicised it without contacting us,” he said. He insisted that the video had nothing to do with LUTH. “For the avoidance of doubt, that viral video has nothing to do with Lagos University Teaching Hospital. It is not LUTH. It could not have been LUTH,” he declared. The CMD disclosed that the hospital currently operates 16 functional dialysis machines, with capacity for 30, providing round-the-clock haemodialysis services to adult and paediatric patients. According to him, the centre recorded approximately 12,500 haemodialysis sessions between January 2022 and October 31, 2026, averaging 2,500 sessions annually and more than 200 monthly. He added that the cumulative downtime of the centre during the period was less than one per cent. Also speaking, Consultant Nephrologist and Deputy Chairman of the Medical Advisory Committee, Prof. Taslim Babawale Bello, described the allegation as medically and technically unfounded, explaining that the dialysis centre was not an admission ward but a specialised facility where patients receive treatment for three to four hours before returning home or to their wards. “It is technically impossible to dialyse a patient on the floor. The dialysis machine requires a specially constructed tubing system to connect to the patient, and its length is limited,” Bello explained. He said strict hygiene and infection-prevention protocols were observed at the centre, adding that even visitors were required to observe protective measures before entering the dialysis area. Bello explained that the centre, which commenced operations in its present building in October 2021, was part of a specialised kidney care complex housing outpatient nephrology clinics, a dedicated pharmacy, laboratory services, consultants’ offices and a kidney transplant facility. He added that the centre had two specialised water treatment units to ensure that water used during dialysis was purified to the required standards. item.title: 2027: No margin for error, INEC warns RECs, sets 6 operational priorities
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Professor Joash Amupitan SAN, has told Resident Electoral Commissioners RECs that “margin for error simply does not exist” in the conduct of the 2027 General Elections. This was as he set six operational priorities for the RECs, from whom he said he expects “immediate, documented compliance and personal accountability.” Amupitan spoke on Wednesday in Abuja at a strategic consultative meeting with the RECs from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory FCT. Reviewing the off-cycle elections since he assumed office in October 2025, Amupitan said the exercises showed “what is achievable when planning starts early, logistics are properly sequenced, and supervision is hands-on.” They covered the governorship elections in Anambra, Ekiti and Osun, the FCT Area Council elections and sixteen legislative bye-elections. He said every bottleneck identified in the off-cycle reviews “must be permanently closed before Saturday’s nationwide simulation and well ahead of January 16.” He cautioned that “general elections operate on an entirely different magnitude and complexity.” The Commission, he said, is managing a verified register of over 100 million voters, including 232,658 Persons With Disabilities who need accessible polling layouts and assistive materials. “In an exercise of that scale, even minor administrative lapses in one state can trigger national headlines and cast doubt on otherwise solid work elsewhere. Margin for error simply does not exist. At this decisive stage of the electoral cycle, the calendar no longer allows for leisurely deliberation or deferred action,” he said. According to him, the Presidential and National Assembly elections will hold on Saturday, January 16, 2027, across 177,299 polling units, followed on Saturday, February 6, 2027, by the Governorship and State Houses of Assembly polls. He described the RECs as “the Commission’s chief operational commanders in the field,” adding that the credibility and public legitimacy of the elections “rest squarely on the precision, vigilance, institutional neutrality, and administrative rigour” with which they lead their state offices. The first priority, he said, is the nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise on Saturday, November 28, 2026, in two polling units per ward. “It is a live operational stress test of our upgraded BVAS devices, our logistics workflows, and our automated result validation safeguards on the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV),” he said, referring to the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS). Every REC, he said, must personally oversee state-level preparations and submit “a comprehensive, candid technical audit” to INEC Headquarters by Monday, November 30, 2026. item.title: Garnacho deletes Aston Villa references from Instagram amid uncertain future
item.description: Chelsea loanee Alejandro Garnacho has removed references to Aston Villa from his Instagram profile amid uncertainty over his future at the Premier League club. The Argentine forward, who joined Villa on loan from Chelsea in July, has struggled to secure regular playing time under manager Unai Emery, making just 95 minutes of appearances across competitions. According to reports, the development attracted attention on Wednesday after fans noticed that the 22 year old had deleted all mentions of Aston Villa from his Instagram page, which has more than 10 million followers. Garnacho’s situation at the club has reportedly become more difficult after Emery left him out of the matchday squad for the third consecutive game on Tuesday night. The Villa manager included two goalkeepers among his substitutes but left one available place on the bench unused. The former Manchester United winger is yet to start a match for the club since his arrival, raising questions about whether he will remain at Villa Park for the duration of his loan spell. Chelsea could also face complications with the arrangement, as they were reportedly hoping to recoup about £42 million from the deal. Garnacho’s limited involvement could make that prospect more difficult. Despite removing Villa references, his Instagram profile reportedly retains several posts relating to Manchester United and Argentina. His FA Cup triumph with United also remains pinned to the top of the page. His situation has drawn comparisons with Liverpool midfielder Harvey Elliott’s loan spell at Aston Villa during the 2025/26 season. Elliott was reportedly sidelined amid concerns that his number of appearances could trigger an obligation-to-buy clause in his loan agreement. Former England midfielder Danny Murphy has also weighed in on Garnacho’s situation, insisting that his exclusion from the team is not a reflection of his footballing ability. item.title: Without Atiku, many Nigerians would’ve lost interest in democracy – Timi Frank
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: A former Deputy National Publicity Secretary of the All Progressives Congress APC, Comrade Timi Frank, has said many Nigerians would have lost interest in democracy without former Vice President Atiku Abubakar’s consistent fight for due process. Frank, a political activist, made the remark in a statement issued on Wednesday in Abuja to mark the 80th birthday of the Presidential Candidate of the African Democratic Congress ADC. “Without you, many Nigerians would have totally lost interest in the democratic process but your courage energised not just a few Nigerians and I believe they (Nigerians across regions) will reward you with massive votes in 2027 general elections,” he said. He described Atiku as an “enduring symbol of democratic resilience, national unity, educational advancement and entrepreneurial excellence.” According to him, reaching the age of 80 is not merely a celebration of longevity but an opportunity for Nigerians to reflect on the former Vice President’s contributions to nation-building and democratic development. Frank said Atiku’s consistent advocacy for democratic governance, political inclusion, constitutionalism, freedom of expression and the protection of democratic institutions had made him an influential figure in the country’s political history. He said the former Vice President’s political journey showed an uncommon belief in healthy political competition, tolerance of divergent opinions and the need for an environment where every Nigerian, irrespective of background, could aspire to leadership. The activist singled out Atiku’s passion for education, describing his investment in the educational development of young Nigerians as one of his most enduring legacies. In his view, Atiku recognised education as a powerful instrument for social transformation, human capital development and national prosperity. Frank also applauded what he called Atiku’s detribalised disposition. “Atiku Abubakar represents a Nigeria where our differences should be sources of strength rather than instruments of division. His disposition towards people from different ethnic and religious backgrounds reinforces the belief that our common humanity and shared national aspirations must always take precedence over primordial considerations,” he said. He praised the former Vice President’s business acumen, describing his journey in the private sector as evidence of entrepreneurial vision, courage and discipline. Frank said Atiku’s contributions to business and education showed that leadership extends beyond occupying public office to creating opportunities, empowering people and investing in institutions that can outlive individuals. The former APC spokesman noted that in recent years Atiku had remained a prominent voice in national conversations on democratic governance, political accountability, economic reforms and the future of Nigeria. item.title: ‘Legends never truly die’ – May Edochie mourns father-in-law Pete
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye May Edochie, the estranged wife of Pete Edochie’s son Yul, has mourned the veteran actor, calling him “an institution” whose legacy will live on. In a glowing tribute shared on Instagram on Wednesday, May recalled that false reports of the veteran actor’s death had circulated over the years, but he had continued working. Pete’s family announced that he died in Enugu at 12:30 a.m. on Wednesday, aged 79, after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. “For so many years, every year, someone somewhere makes a false announcement of your death but you kept going with strength to continue working,” she wrote. View this post on Instagram A post shared by May Yul-Edochie (@mayyuledochie) Reflecting on his death, May said: “One moment, there is life; the next, eternity calls. Such is the fragility of human existence. We make plans, hold conversations, nurse expectations and believe there will always be another day, until life reminds us that tomorrow is never promised.” Calling him the “Lion of Africa,” she said his passing reminded her that “beyond all, the opinions, the misunderstandings and the stories that life sometimes throws around, we are all humans, and death has a way of reminding us of what truly matters.” May also said she would remember Pete as a veteran whose name, voice, presence and contributions to Nollywood would remain unforgettable. “You were an institution, a father figure to many and a man whose legacy will outlive his earthly years,” she wrote. “One thing is certain: legends never truly die; they live on through the memories they create and the impact they leave behind.” She also prayed for Pete’s wife, Josephine, and other relatives, writing: “To mummy and the rest of us you have left behind, may the good Lord strengthen through Christ our Lord.” She ended the tribute with prayers for the deceased: “God rest your soul Ononenyi!” Vanguard News The post ‘Legends never truly die’ – May Edochie mourns father-in-law Pete appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: My finances were better before Tinubu’s tenure – Seyi Law
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigerian comedian, Seyi Law, has admitted that his personal finances were in a better state before President Bola Tinubu assumed office, despite defending the administration’s economic policies and urging Nigerians to endure the hardship associated with them. The comedian made the remarks during an appearance on the Charity Zone Podcast, where he argued that the benefits of some government policies might take years to become evident. Seyi Law, a known supporter of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), said economic policies often come with immediate difficulties before producing long term gains. Using China as an example, he said the country’s emergence as a major global economy involved significant sacrifices. “For China to be where they are today, if they tell you the number of Chinese who died, you won’t believe,” he said. When asked whether Nigerians must die before enjoying the benefits of the country’s economic policies, the comedian clarified that people would have to experience the hardship resulting from such decisions before the expected gains could materialise. “No. You must feel the pain of the policy to reap the benefit of it. Every good policy that becomes good stabilises after 10 to 12 years,” he said. Despite his defence of the government, Seyi Law acknowledged the economic difficulties facing many Nigerians, admitting that people were struggling to afford basic necessities. “People are hungry. I will be a hypocrite, a bad person to say people are not hungry,” he said. He also spoke about how the rising cost of living had affected his ability to support family members living in the United Kingdom. According to him, an amount that previously covered their needs now requires a significantly higher sum, forcing him to increase his financial support. “My finances were better before this government came in. My family are in the UK and then with N1.2 million they are okay, but now I have had to double that to like N4.5 million every other month,” he added. The post My finances were better before Tinubu’s tenure – Seyi Law appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Guardiola says next coaching job will be with national team
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Pep Guardiola says he will manage a national team when he returns to coaching after turning down an offer to take charge of Italy because he felt he needed a break from football. In an interview reported by Reuters, Guardiola told his former Barcelona teammate Romario that he had spoken with the Italian Football Federation but was not ready to take another job. “It was one of the greatest honours I’ve had, that they thought of me to coach Italy. But it came at a time when I needed to stop,” he said. “If it had happened a year or two earlier, I probably would have accepted.” The Spaniard said the approach came when Paolo Maldini and Leonardo, whom he described as people he loved dearly, reached out to him. He added that he did not know how long his break would last. “Right now I feel very well,” Guardiola told former Brazil forward Romario. “But if I return to football one day, it will be when my stomach tells me it’s the right time.” Guardiola left Manchester City at the end of last season after a decade in charge. He won six Premier League titles, including four in succession, three FA Cups, five League Cups and the Champions League. In the same interview, Guardiola said Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo’s rivalry helped prolong both players’ careers. The pair won a combined 13 Ballon d’Or awards and dominated football for more than a decade, including during their spells at Barcelona and Real Madrid. “If Messi hadn’t had Cristiano, or if Cristiano hadn’t had Messi, their careers would likely have been shorter,” Guardiola said. “They had each other in their rearview mirrors, watching what the other was doing made them think: ‘I want to be better than him, I want to win more than him,’” Guardiola, who coached Messi for four seasons at Barcelona, credited the forward for much of his success there. He led the Spanish club to 14 trophies, including two Champions League titles and three La Liga crowns. “Messi! When you have such good players, you become good yourself,” Guardiola said when asked what helped him win so many titles. item.title: Most Nigerians support political violence when opponents are victims — Shehu Sani
item.description: Former Kaduna Central Senator, Shehu Sani, has accused Nigerians of condoning political violence when it is directed at opponents, warning that the attitude is fuelling attacks on political supporters across the country. Sani said many Nigerians encourage violence against people whose political choices or opinions differ from theirs, rather than condemn such acts irrespective of the victims’ affiliations. He stated this on X on Wednesday following the campaign violence that reportedly left four persons dead in Delta State. Condemning the killings, Sani said Nigerians were more likely to support or excuse political violence when those attacked belonged to opposing political camps. “The political violence in Delta State has led to the death of four supporters of Senator Omo Agege of the NDC. A condemnable act. However, we are shying away from the truth that most Nigerians are fully in support of political violence as long as the victims are in the opposite camp,” he wrote. He argued that people who support violence against political opponents often fail to recognise that such acts could eventually affect their own side. “Most people encourage and support mob or thuggish acts against those they differ with in political choices or opinions. Those aiding and abetting political violence are feeding a Tiger with the thought that it will only consume their political adversaries,” Sani said. The former senator also criticised the media’s handling of reports of political attacks, accusing some media organisations of using descriptions that downplay the severity of violence depending on the political affiliation of those involved. He cited reports of attacks involving former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar in Kebbi and President Bola Tinubu in Abuja, saying some media outlets used different descriptions for incidents involving the two political figures. “Some media Houses have even crafted a beautiful way of reporting political violence…POLITICAL THUGS attacked Atiku in Kebbi while ANGRY YOUTHS attacked Tinubu at Abuja Mosque,” he added. Sani’s comments come amid growing concerns over political violence and intolerance ahead of the 2027 general elections, with incidents involving political supporters raising questions about the safety of campaign activities and the role of political parties in preventing attacks. The post Most Nigerians support political violence when opponents are victims — Shehu Sani appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Tinubu has fulfilled promise made to Igbo after civil war – Kalu
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe, Umuahia Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Hon. Benjamin Kalu, has said that President Bola Tinubu has fulfilled the promise made to the Igbo after the civil war in 1970. He noted that at the end of the civil war, the federal government had announced the policy of Reconciliation, Reconstruction and Rehabilitation to rebuild Igbo land, alleging that successive administrations failed to implement the policy. The Deputy Speaker stated that Tinubu is the only president that has made meaningful efforts in implementing the policy by establishing the South East Development Commission (SEDC) and putting up infrastructural projects and political appointments across the South East zone. Kalu, who stated this in Umuahia during the donation of 25 vehicles to the Abia State chapter of the Door to Door mobilisation by High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, urged the Igbo to re-elect the president to finish his job in the next four years. “For over 50 years, nobody was able to fulfil the promise made to the Igbo after the civil war. Gone are the days of promise. Today, President Bola Tinubu has fulfilled the promise he has given the South East Development Commission (SEDC). He has also given the SEDC the permission to open what is known as the South East Investment Company. And he has funded the company with billions of Naira. “Today, the company has started the project of piping gas across the Southeast. The companies in Lagos and Kano will start coming to build in the Southeast. This is the president that Tompolo wants us to support. “Across the South East, more roads are springing up because our son is the Minister of Works, Engr Dave Umahi. I can’t remember the last time an Igbo man was the Minister of Works. Umahi has been making us proud. The President also appointed Ojukwu as the Minister of Foreign Affairs and another Igbo as the Chief of Naval Staff. The Minister of State for Finance is also an Igbo. “The President has also invested money in securing our lives and properties. The Ministry of Defence budget has increased; employment in the military and police is increasing. The president has also supported state police. Salaries are not being owed because Tinubu removed the fuel subsidy and released more money for the sub-nations. He urged the Igbo to reject anyone who is campaigning for the South East zone to serve for only a four-year term, stressing that when the time comes, the zone would take eight years, as others have done. “Reject them when they come to you that they have signed an agreement for the Igbo to serve for only four years. The Igbo will not wait after 60 years to receive power for only four years. We didn’t wait for 60 years for the Igbo to take only half the bread. Other zones have done right years; when the time comes, the Igbo will take eight years, not four years.” The post 2027: Tinubu has fulfilled promise made to Igbo after civil war – Kalu appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Osubi Airport simulates air crash after 20 years
item.description: …Drill identifies emergency response gaps, need for modern equipment By Egufe Yafugborhi WARRI — The Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), Alfred Diete-Spiff Airport, Osubi, Delta State, has conducted its first simulated aircraft crash rescue exercise in about 20 years to assess its emergency response capabilities and identify areas requiring improvement. The exercise, conducted at about 1:30pm on the airport’s airside, simulated an aircraft crash involving passengers who sustained varying degrees of injuries. Several emergency response agencies participated in the drill, including the Nigerian Navy Hospital and Air Station Fire Service, Nigeria Police Force, Delta State Fire Service, Nigerian Red Cross Society, Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB), Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Delta Procare Hospital, Nigerian Ports Authority Health Service and Renaissance Africa Energy Fire Service. Speaking after the exercise, the Airport Manager, Winston Egwuatu, expressed satisfaction with the outcome, saying identified operational gaps would be addressed to strengthen the airport’s emergency response capacity. He explained that the exercise was designed to test the preparedness of personnel, availability of equipment and effectiveness of established emergency procedures. “No simulation exercise is perfect. It was actually meant to test the preparedness of both the officers who are going to be deployed, the materials and also the procedures. “The purpose of this is to identify the gaps and close them, so that when it is deployed, we will deploy better,” he said. Egwuatu, who spoke alongside departmental heads, said observers from the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) identified areas requiring improvement, particularly personnel training and retraining. He noted that the airport had recorded operational improvements since its transition from an airstrip but stressed the need for additional operational vehicles and modern firefighting equipment. “Within resources available to the management of the airport, we have done very well. This airport used to be an airstrip. Now it’s operating as an airport. That means there have been some level of upgrade. “However, there is need for improvement in regards to operational vehicles and state-of-the-art fire tankers to meet the time that we find ourselves now,” he said. The airport manager disclosed that observations from the exercise would be compiled into a comprehensive report to guide corrective measures and requests requiring intervention from higher authorities. He also emphasised the importance of effective collaboration among emergency response agencies, noting that prompt intervention could determine survival during an aircraft accident. “It is in the interest of everybody to deploy, all of us who have the wherewithal to not just respond, but respond timely. item.title: ‘Incoming President’, Titi celebrates Atiku, says ex-VP not tired at 80
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Wife of the former Vice President, Atiku Abubakar, has described her husband as the “incoming President of Nigeria” as he turned 80 on Wednesday, saying he is “not tired” and that his vision for the country is “even clearer.” In a birthday tribute titled “Daddy at 80”, Chief Amina Titi Atiku Abubakar, the former Second Lady of Nigeria, said she was celebrating “the Incoming President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria come May 29th, 2027 by the Special Grace of God.” “At 80, you are not tired. At 80, your vision for Nigeria is even clearer. I have walked with you through valleys and mountains, and I know what God has placed in you for Nigeria,” she wrote. She said Nigeria needed his “experience,” his “capacity, and your compassionate heart now more than ever.” According to her, this is “reflecting in the enthusiastic and passionate ways Nigerians turned out to cheer you to victory as you articulate your policies and canvass support for your presidential aspiration come January 16, 2027.” Titi said the milestone coincided with 57 years of marriage. “Eighty years of a life well-lived and Fifty-seven years of a love that has stood the test of time. When I first met you as a young lady, I saw a cute, handsome, principled, brilliant, focused Customs officer with big dreams. I did not know I was meeting a destiny.” She credited her husband with the support that led her into the campaign against human trafficking. “Many men would have stopped their wife from confronting human trafficking. You did not. You not only gave me the wings to fly, but the inspiration, the courage, the confidence and the wherewithal to fight for humanity and the vulnerables. You told me, ‘Titi, go and save those girls.'” She said the Women Trafficking and Child Labour Eradication Foundation (WOTCLEF) was born from that encouragement in 1999. “A law was made to criminalize human trafficking in Nigeria and NAPTIP was established to save millions. “The woman I am today – the Lecturer, the Advocate, the Amazing Amazon, the Former Second Lady of Nigeria, the Grand Matron to several Organizations – I am because you allowed me to become,” she said. Titi also paid tribute to Atiku’s record in public service. “Nigeria has known you as a diligent Customs Officer, a successful businessman, a two-term Vice President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria who chaired the National Economic Council that paid off the country’s foreign debt and a democrat who has kept faith with democracy even when it was costly. You don’t just make promises; you build systems. You don’t just talk about privatization and jobs; you did it. “Only few people know how many school fees you pay silently; how many widows you feed daily; how many young people you gave jobs in and out of government, how many lives you have touched directly or indirectly and how many destinies you have transformed positively. item.title: Nollywood Stars Joke Silva, Funke Akindele, Others Pay Tribute To Pete Edochie
item.description: Nollywood stars Joke Silva, Funke Akindele, Mercy Johnson and others have paid tributes to veteran actor Pete Edochie, who died Wednesday after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer at the age of 79. The actor’s death was announced by his son, Chief Leo Pete Edochie, who confirmed that he died at 12:30 a.m. on November 25, 2026, in Enugu, Nigeria. His death has sparked an outpouring of tributes from colleagues, public leaders and entertainers who have celebrated his remarkable career, influence and legacy. Actress Joke Silva expressed sadness over his death, remembering his playful side. “Uncle Pete…I will miss your teasing. Rest well Sir,” she wrote. Filmmaker and actress Funke Akindele recalled growing up watching Edochie in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart , before eventually sharing the screen with him in the film Egg of Life . She expressed gratitude for his encouragement and the impact he made on younger generations of actors. “Thank you for paving the way for so many of us in Nollywood and for being an inspiration to us over the years. Your work lives on,” she wrote. Similarly, actress Uche Jombo described Edochie as one of Nollywood’s greatest pillars, a master of his craft and a custodian of Nigerian culture. She said the late actor “gave Nigerian storytelling a face, a voice and a legacy that will outlive generations.” “His contribution to Nollywood cannot be measured by the number of films he appeared in, but by the impact he made, the standards he set and the generations of actors he inspired.” Actress Omoni Oboli described his passing as the fall of an iroko tree, writing, “Hmmm 2026! It is well. The Iroko has fallen. Rest in power sir Pete Edochie.” May Edochie, the estranged wife of the late actor’s son, Yul Edochie, also paid tribute, describing him as an institution and a father figure to many. She reflected on the false reports of his death that had circulated over the years, noting that he had continued working despite the rumours. Actor Charles Inojie paid tribute using several of the late actor’s traditional praise names, including Ebube Dike, Ntu Mara Igwe and King of the Forests, before praying for his peaceful rest. While DJ Kaywise thanked him for his contributions to the industry, other entertainers who expressed their grief included comedian Sabinus, who described Edochie as an oracle and a legend. Pete Edochie was born on March 7, 1947, in Zaria, Kaduna State. His ancestral roots, however, trace back to Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, in Anambra State. Edochie rose to prominence through his portrayal of Okonkwo in the 1987 Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart . His commanding screen presence, distinctive voice, and memorable delivery of traditional proverbs subsequently made him one of Nollywood’s most recognisable figures. item.title: Ebola Fight Runs Up Against Customs, Rites In Remote DR Congo
item.description: For health workers in the volatile eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), tackling local suspicions is as big a problem as combating the Ebola virus that has plagued it for six months. In the rural community of Bulambo-Isale, AFP saw a small crowd gather this week along a dirt track, determined to prevent an ambulance bringing the body of a local Ebola victim for burial. Victims of the highly contagious haemorrhagic fever, which spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids, must be interred in sealed body bags to prevent infection spreading from the corpse. Burial ceremonies are conducted by specially trained health workers, anonymous in protective hazmat suits, some of whom locals allege are brought in from outside the community and do not speak the local languages. In this file photo taken on March 09, 2019 Health workers are seen inside the ‘red zone’ of an Ebola treatment centre, which was attacked in the early hours of the morning in Butembo. – Democratic Republic of Congo’s government on June 25, 2020 officially declared an end to an epidemic of Ebola that broke out in the east of the troubled country in August 2018 and went on to claim 2,277 lives. (Photo by JOHN WESSELS / AFP) But custom dictates that the deceased be buried by their own family and their body be allowed to fuse with the earth of their ancestors. “The authorities have imposed the Ebola response on locals without first making sure how they interpret it,” grumbled Patricien Kambale, who became a livestock farmer after university. “The sick victim gets carted away in a vehicle and locals don’t know where they’re being taken. Then we learn later that the person has died so locals think the doctors are using poisoned medicine to kill people,” he said. Suspicions of ‘profiteering’ Health workers in Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) simulate with the help of an Outbreak Response Advisor admission protocols of suspected cases during a training by medical charity, Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) to reinforce regional emergency response capacity for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo Locals say they are distrustful of Congolese authorities, who have a reputation for corruption and nepotism. Left to cope with the miseries inflicted by myriad armed groups that have stalked their mineral-rich region for more than three decades, they fear their customs and lives matter little to the powers that be. Wilson Kasyani, chief doctor for the Vuhovi health district that includes Bulambo-Isale, a rural settlement in North Kivu province, was worried for the ambulance and its occupants. “Weapons are everywhere” in the mountainous region, he said. Medical workers face almost daily attacks due to locals’ hostility to efforts to respond to the Ebola outbreak, which has killed more than 5,000 people out of more than 11,000 cases since May. “Today, people entered a nurse’s home and wounded her son,” Kasyani said wearily. “And yesterday we had to stop someone who wanted to attack invest
